messages:
maria-ops: FYI ACME support ticket says they saw a cluster of 500s + 'auth failed' around 2026-12-01 22:12 UTC. They're asking whether our audit logs contain request bodies and if the KMS/HSM rotation during that window could have impacted log availability/access. Need scope + timeline so CS can respond.

raj-support: Ticket SUP-4921. I can share the top request IDs and timestamps. Do we have a known KMS rotation around that time?

oliver-sec: Can you paste the req_ids? We'll check audit ingestion and KMS rotate logs. If bodies were captured unredacted that's a compliance hit.

maria-ops: req_ids: 0a1b2c3, 0a1b2c4, 0a1b2c5. Errors show 500 w/ message 'kv-cache: decrypt failed' then retries. Also saw latency spikes ~300-900ms before 500s.

oliver-sec: Quick initial read: those timestamps line up with a KMS rotation batch that had a brief propagation delay. Our audit pipeline writes metadata-only by default (payload_redacted=true), but will run a full check for that prefix/time range.

anne-customer-success: Customer is specifically worried about message content. Please confirm ASAP if any plaintext request bodies ended up in audit logs — they want written confirmation if so.

oliver-sec: Running the query now. If we find plaintext captures it'll be a P1 compliance escalation. ETA ~90m. @sec-bot please start HSM/KMS rotation audit and log-access trail for that window.

sec-bot: HSM-audit job started (job_id: hsm-audit-2026-17954). Notified: oliver-sec, devops-bot.

devops-bot: KMS rotation job 17954 shows a 3-minute drift window (22:11 - 22:14 UTC). No rotate failures flagged, but key-propagation TTL noted in logs.

oliver-sec: Query complete: ingestion service wrote audit entries with metadata only. No request bodies found under audit-s3/acme-prod/2026-12-01/22:12.*. Sample log line: ```timestamp=2026-12-01T22:12:05Z service=audit request_id=0a1b2c3 user_id=acct-ACME action=invoke_model payload_redacted=true```

raj-support: Can you confirm this across regions? ACME uses eu-west-1 + us-west-2.

oliver-sec: Confirmed: both regions show payload_redacted=true for the matching req_ids. The 'decrypt failed' looks to be a temporary KMS client refresh race, not a key compromise or HSM error.

maria-ops: Great. Customer also wants a timeline and if they should be notified. What's our notification policy here?

oliver-sec: Since there's no evidence of plaintext capture or key compromise, this is internal-only. Recommended action: send an explanation to ACME that a short KMS propagation delay caused transient decrypt errors and 5xxs; audit logs contain metadata only. Offer the matched req_ids and remediation steps. No legal escalation required.

anne-customer-success: Please include exact timestamps, affected req_ids, confirmation of no plaintext capture, and remediation steps. They may request a call.

oliver-sec: Drafting now — will post in #customer-comm-drafts. TL;DR: window 2026-12-01 22:11–22:14 UTC, KMS propagation delay ~3m, affected ~0.02% of ACME's requests, no plaintext in audit logs, mitigation applied (client backoff + rotation checks). Offer 1:1 call.

raj-support: I'll relay to the customer and attach the req_ids + security draft. Note: the retries produced extra token usage; any billing/SLA recourse?

maria-ops: Per support policy, increased token usage from system errors is eligible for credit. I'll loop in billing if ACME requests compensation.

oliver-sec: Post-incident follow-up created: add KMS client backoff, enforce rotate propagation check, add alert for decrypt error spike. Owner: eng-infra (raj-support). ETA: 2 weeks.

maria-ops: :thumbsup: Thanks all — I'll update the customer and close the loop once they ACK.

anne-customer-success: :eyes: Keep me posted. I'll only escalate to legal if the draft recommends it.
